briefing.text: The cohort is a mixed head-and-neck MSK-IMPACT set (HNSCC, salivary tumours, skin and others; 151 samples). NOTCH1 in HNSCC is mostly loss-of-function, so NOTCH1 rates computed over all samples do not describe ACC. Identify ACC with ONCOTREE_CODE (ACYC = adenoid cystic carcinoma) / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED in data_clinical_sample.txt, run every test on ACC samples only, and report the ACC n.
briefing.reason: Analysing the whole cohort would mix in HNSCC NOTCH1 biology and answer a different question.

briefing.text: Not every NOTCH1 mutation is activating. In ACC, activating NOTCH1 mutations are missense or in-frame changes in the heterodimerization (HD) domain (about aa 1570-1730, exons 26-27), or truncating/frameshift mutations in or just before the C-terminal PEST domain (about aa >2400, exon 34) that remove PEST. EGF-repeat mutations are not counted as activating. List each ACC NOTCH1 variant with HGVSp and protein position, classify it by domain, and drop Silent/Intron/UTR classes. Use activating NOTCH1 as the primary variable and any nonsynonymous NOTCH1 as a sensitivity analysis.
briefing.reason: The hypothesis is about activating mutations specifically, so how variants are classified determines the counts.

briefing.text: 'Metastatic ACC' can mean either that the sequenced specimen is a metastasis (SAMPLE_TYPE / sequenced site) or that the patient has distant metastatic disease (DISTANT_METS, DISEASE_EXTENT). A primary-tumour sample from a patient with distant metastases is metastatic at the patient level. Cross-tabulate these columns for ACC samples, use patient-level distant-metastasis status as the main grouping, also report the sample-type comparison, and check whether the two agree. Note whether either grouping leaves a usable comparison group.
briefing.reason: The two definitions can give different groups, and one of them may be nearly degenerate, which changes what can be tested inside the data.

briefing.text: A NOTCH1-wildtype call only counts if NOTCH1 was profiled. Confirm in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt that each ACC sample's panel covers NOTCH1 (IMPACT341/410/468 should), and drop unprofiled samples from the denominator. Some NOTCH1 activation comes from rearrangements or CNAs, so grep data_sv.txt and data_cna.txt for NOTCH1 in ACC samples. In a sensitivity analysis, count only clearly activating SVs (e.g. 3' rearrangements that keep the intracellular domain).
briefing.reason: Gets the denominator right and catches non-SNV activation events.

briefing.text: Samples sequenced without a matched normal (SOMATIC_STATUS=Unmatched) can report germline NOTCH1 variants as somatic. For ACC NOTCH1 carriers, tabulate SOMATIC_STATUS and VAF = t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count). Flag likely germline variants (VAF near 50% or 100%, especially in low-purity tumours) and rerun without them as a sensitivity analysis.
briefing.reason: When counts are this small, one false carrier can change the comparison.

briefing.text: The ACC subgroup is small, so Fisher's exact p-values can be above 0.05 even when an enrichment is real and large. Report counts, proportions in each group, the odds ratio with CI, and the p-value. Do not treat a non-significant p-value by itself as evidence against the claim. Weigh the direction and size of the effect, and read 'contradicts' as a clearly reversed direction.
briefing.reason: This keeps lack of power from being mistaken for contradicting evidence, which is a likely interpretation error here.

briefing.text: Prior literature, from library domain knowledge only (not verified this run): activating NOTCH1 mutations occur in about 10-15% of unselected/mostly primary ACC series (Stephens 2013 JCI; Ho 2013 Nat Genet) and about 25-26% of recurrent/metastatic ACC series (Ho 2019 Nat Genet; Ferrarotto 2017 JCO). NOTCH1-mutant ACC has been linked to solid histology, bone/liver metastasis and worse survival. If the within-data comparison cannot be made (e.g. one group is nearly empty), the ACC NOTCH1 rate in this cohort can be compared against these reference rates. State clearly which kind of evidence decided the label.
briefing.reason: The task allows deciding from established biology when the tables cannot test the claim directly, and these reference rates are the external comparator.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed the right comparator is an external primary-ACC NOTCH1 rate recalled from memory (about 10-15%), and that the published primary series used the same variant definition, panel and cohort selection as this targeted-panel cohort. Neither team tested this.

Both teams assumed the patient-level lifetime DISTANT_METS flag is the right 'metastatic' variable, not the specimen-level SAMPLE_TYPE or SITE_SEQUENCED. The specimen-level split points the other way (team-b: 4/12 primaries vs 3/24 metastases).
Both assumed that 'enriched in metastatic ACC' means a higher rate in metastatic than in non-metastatic ACC, not a link to a pattern of metastatic spread (which organ) within metastatic disease.
unused_evidence: METASTATIC_SITE / DETAILED_METASTATIC_SITE (lung 13, liver 3, bone 2, pleura 2, brain 1, skin 1 among ACYC). Library facts already link NOTCH1-mutant ACC to bone/liver spread, and neither team tabulated NOTCH1 by metastatic organ.
DISTANT_METASTASIS_PATHOLOGIC_SPREAD and SITE_OF_RECURRENCE, which describe where and how widely each patient's disease spread, independent of which specimen was sequenced.

Patient-level histology and outcome fields (Tumor Sample Histology / WHO Class, Overall Survival, Disease Free, DISEASE_EXTENT). These are what a source study would use to show NOTCH1-mutant ACC is the more aggressive subtype.
MYB-NFIB FISH and TUMOR_PURITY. Purity changes how sensitive the assay is for NOTCH1 in metastatic versus primary specimens.
unresolved_weak_points: Team-a: the external baseline (~12%) was not verified. Team-a reported this weakness but did not resolve it, and no sensitivity analysis across baseline values was reported.

Team-b: the binomial test against the baseline is borderline (p=0.06) for activating variants, and the specimen-level comparison runs the other way. Team-b reported both and resolved neither; it kept the patient-level framing without an internal test.
second_readings: 'Enriched in metastatic ACCs' could mean enriched in metastatic specimens compared with primary specimens (the SAMPLE_TYPE split). On that reading the internal data point the other way.
It could mean enriched among patients with distant metastasis at particular sites (liver/bone versus lung-only), which the metastatic-site columns could test internally.
'Activating' could mean HD-domain/PEST-type changes only (team-b, 19%) or any nonsynonymous NOTCH1 variant (team-a, 31%). The choice moves the rate relative to any baseline.
challenge.verdict: Moderate trust. Both teams rest the label on a recalled external baseline, with no internal comparator. Their own specimen-level split points the other way, and neither used the metastatic-site, histology or survival columns that could give an internal test.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your method counts any nonsynonymous NOTCH1 variant as activating. If you restrict to HD-domain and PEST/C-terminal truncating variants and redo the binomial test across baselines from 10% to 15%, does the evidence for enrichment still hold, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You did not use METASTATIC_SITE, DETAILED_METASTATIC_SITE or DISTANT_METASTASIS_PATHOLOGIC_SPREAD. If you cross-tabulate NOTCH1 status in the 36 ACYC patients by organ of distant spread (for example lung-only vs liver/bone), do you get an internal comparison that changes or replaces the external-baseline test?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your specimen-level split is 5/12 primaries vs 6/24 metastases. When you run Fisher's exact test on it, and on Overall/Disease-Free survival by NOTCH1 status, does the internal evidence agree with or contradict the external-baseline result, and how do you weigh the two?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your activating-only test is borderline (p=0.06). If you tabulate activating NOTCH1 by METASTATIC_SITE / DISTANT_METASTASIS_PATHOLOGIC_SPREAD, and by Tumor Sample Histology / WHO Class, do you find an internal contrast strong enough to change the label or its confidence?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: When you compare TUMOR_PURITY and NOTCH1 VAF between primary and metastatic ACYC specimens, can a difference in assay sensitivity explain the opposite direction you saw at specimen level (4/12 vs 3/24)? Does that change which level of analysis you rely on?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Does your 10-15% baseline refer to activating NOTCH1 only or to any NOTCH1 variant? If you test your activating count and your any-variant count each against the baseline that matches its definition, do the two conclusions agree?

In published genomic studies of adenoid cystic carcinoma, what fraction of primary (non-recurrent, non-metastatic) tumours carry NOTCH1 mutations, and is that fraction reported for all NOTCH1 variants or only activating ones?
questions.why: Both teams' enrichment claim depends entirely on this baseline, which they recalled from memory, and the two teams' variant definitions differ.

questions.question: Which NOTCH1 mutation classes (HD-domain missense/in-frame, PEST or C-terminal truncations, or others) are conventionally classified as activating in solid tumours such as adenoid cystic carcinoma?
questions.why: The two teams' definitions give rates of 19% vs 31%, and the definition decides whether the comparison with the baseline is significant.

findings.question: Which NOTCH1 mutation classes (HD-domain missense/in-frame, PEST or C-terminal truncations, or others) are conventionally classified as activating in solid tumours such as adenoid cystic carcinoma?
findings.answer: NOT SETTLED BY WEB: the gateway returned HTTP 403. From recall only, two classes are conventionally activating: (a) missense or in-frame indels in the heterodimerization (HD) domain (~aa 1570-1730), and (b) nonsense/frameshift truncations in or just before the PEST domain (C-terminal, ~aa >=2400) that remove the PEST degron. 3' rearrangements that keep NICD also count. EGF-repeat missense mutations and truncations upstream of the transmembrane domain are loss-of-function (the HNSCC/cSCC pattern) and are not activating. Ferrarotto et al. JCO 2017 used this HD/PEST definition.
